note: Tier reasoning lives in the prose. Only these example names go stale — update this one file.

tier1.name: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small
tier1.detail: 8,191 token limit · 1,536 dims · ~$0.02 / 1M tokens. The -large sibling: same limit, 3,072 dims, ~6× the price.

tier2.name: Cohere embed-v4.0
tier2.detail: 128K token context · 1,536 dims (configurable to 256) · multimodal · $0.12 / 1M. Voyage voyage-4-large is comparable.

tier3.name: Voyage voyage-context-4
tier3.detail: up to 120K token context. Cohere embed-v4.0 also qualifies at 128K.

tier4.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
tier4.detail: 384 dims, runs on CPU. Jina jina-embeddings-v3 is stronger (8,192 tokens, 1,024 dims) but CC-BY-NC — commercial self-hosting needs a licence.

tier5.name: Cohere embed-v4.0
tier5.detail: 100+ languages, small cross-language quality gap. Google gemini-embedding-001 is an alternative.

tier1.name: Claude Opus 5 · GPT-5.6 · Gemini 3.1 Pro
tier1.detail: maximum reasoning — multi-hop questions, code, high-stakes summarisation, at low query volume.

tier2.name: Claude Sonnet 5 · mid-tier GPT-5.x · Gemini 3.1 Pro (standard)
tier2.detail: the default production choice: read 3–5 chunks, answer faithfully, cite.

tier3.name: Claude Haiku 4.5 · Gemini 3.5 Flash
tier3.detail: high-QPS surfaces, and the routing / rewriting steps that are just small classifications.

tier4.name: Llama / Mistral open-weight lines
tier4.detail: on-prem / air-gapped, or answering from a fixed small corpus. Check current release names — they move fast.

fixedFacts: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small and -large both cap at 8,191 input tokens. Not 1,048. This number has held across ada-002 and the whole v3 generation.
